requirements: Verify fork head and contributor ancestry. Capture commands, exit codes, fresh logs and JUnit XML with test counts, failures and skips.

Run ./gradlew :solr:core:cleanTest :solr:core:test --tests org.apache.solr.update.SolrCmdDistributorTest, with a recorded seed; repeat the focused stall method under multiple seeds. Run ./gradlew tidy and ./gradlew check -x test. A tracked formatting change needs a committed successor and new exact-head gate.

In a disposable checkout at this head, revert only the production change in StreamingSolrClients while leaving the test unchanged; show the focused test fails at the intended assertion after its preconditions execute. Capture source diff, logs and XML. Compile/setup failure, timeout or skip is not fail-before proof.

Resolve the active stalled-runner risk before a clean verdict. With controlled synchronization, establish whether after a stall is reported queued updates and callbacks can continue and whether a subsequent delete-by-query or commit can overtake them. Compare with the contributor parent and baseline as appropriate, record exact source changes, observations and evidence. If a correctness defect is confirmed, do not mark this head clean: hand back for a scoped implementation, permanent regression and superseding gate. If not reproduced, explain exactly what was established and remaining limits; non-reproduction alone is not proof of safety.

The test uses a non-retrying failing node to establish error retention. Existing retry tests do not establish retry while another client stalls. Explicitly assess that path and report any gap; do not claim it was proven without a test.
verdict_policy: Positive checks and valid fail-before are required. An unresolved material stalled-runner safety concern prevents a clean PR verdict. This head contains no production lifecycle repair. Do not post publicly.
